title: Pasta alla Norma
subtitle: Sicilian pasta with aubergine and tomato
excerpt: A Sicilian classic built on fried aubergine, a quick tomato sauce, and salty ricotta on top. The aubergine needs proper heat and time to go golden, so do not rush that step. Everything else comes together fast.
sourceNotes: Based on the classic Sicilian dish pasta alla norma, which traditionally uses salted ricotta as the finishing cheese.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead and kept in the fridge.

content.text: Salted ricotta is the traditional topping, but if you cannot find it, finely grated parmesan works well. Fry the aubergine in batches so the pan stays hot; crowding it leads to steaming rather than browning.

Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Fry the aubergine cubes in batches for 8 to 10 minutes total, turning occasionally, until deep golden on most sides. Season with salt and set aside.
In the same pan, add the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil. Cook the garlic and chilli flakes over a medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon. Season with salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened slightly.
Meanwhile, cook the rigatoni in a large saucepan of salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.
Return the aubergine to the sauce and stir to combine.
Add the drained pasta to the sauce with a splash of pasta water and toss over the heat for 1 minute.
Scatter over the basil leaves and serve with crumbled ricotta or grated parmesan on top.

items.cause: Pan was overcrowded or heat too low
items.fix: Fry in smaller batches over high heat.
Keep simmering until the sauce thickens and coats a spoon.
